description: next/ v4 — PHASE-0 ARCHITECTURE FIX: REAL ERP OperationsResponse (Level-3 IST/actual feedback) via the sim-v5 ERP REST API (http://192.168.178.154:38260/api/confirmations), replacing the postgresql/erp-operations-response.json direct-erpdb poller (erpdb.llm_test_v3.order_confirmations — the forbidden direct-DB bypass). Same sourceId (edge SOURCE_IDS unchanged), same profile contract (SMProfile-OperationsResponse). production_order_no = join key (cross-rule join + kgIdProperty; RESPONDS_TO ProductionOrder on the same key). confirmed_qty -> quantity_produced drives the qty_shortfall cross-rule against ProductionOrder.qty_planned. cycle_time_actual -> cycle_time_actual_sec (the real actual cycle time). ts_end -> actual_end_time + completed_at (the REST confirmation's end timestamp is the actual completion time; the old postgres source used confirmation_time for both). recorded_at -> updated_at. /api/confirmations has NO status column, but every confirmation IS a completion -> status bound to the constant 'fertig' ({ const: 'fertig', smAttribute: 'status' }) so the OperationsResponse contract is complete. NOTE 2026-07-12: the three cross-rules that gated on this attribute (qty_shortfall, material_unavailable, late_delivery) are RETIRED — a when-guard over a source-bound constant can never discriminate (see their tombstones and ci/lint-cross-constraints.mjs, which fails the build on any ACTIVE rule with such a guard). The constant stays for contract completeness; it MUST NOT be used as a when-guard operand. full_refresh change-detection (the REST API does not honour ?since — verified) — it-edge dedups via the per-id HWM on production_order_no. filter=null (full confirmation set per the cutover decision). machine_no/machine_id are null on the current confirmation feed (BDE bridge does not stamp the machine) — mapped for forward-compat; the ON_MACHINE edge resolves once the feed carries it. scrap_qty/good_qty/operator_id unmapped (not in the profile contract). --- 2026-08-03, THE status CONSTANT IS REMOVED. It bound every OperationsResponse to the literal 'fertig' and therefore asserted, on every record, that the operation was COMPLETE. MEASURED live: 34715 operations_response events reached central-ts in three hours and ALL of them carried status='fertig'. That is a false statement at scale, not a harmless placeholder. I LOOKED FOR A REAL FIELD TO DERIVE IT FROM AND THERE IS NONE. /api/confirmations carries no status column (0 of 5000 rows). The only candidate was final_confirmation, and it is a CONSTANT TOO: measured over the COMPLETE prod population, logistics.bde_confirmations holds 2,038,771 rows and final_confirmation is false on every single one — never true, not once. The `shift` column is NULL on all 2,038,772. So a valueMap would have swapped one constant for another while looking like a derivation. THE ATTRIBUTE IS NOW ABSENT, WHICH IS THE HONEST OUTCOME: a consumer reads no status and reports none, exactly as mappings/machine-identity.json allows erpMachineRef:null so a consumer greys instead of guessing. Absent is not the same class of error as wrong. THE ROOT CAUSE IS UPSTREAM AND IS NOT FIXED HERE: a BDE system in which no confirmation is EVER final never reports an operation complete — the same family as production orders that never go terminal. Deciding WHEN a confirmation becomes final (last operation? planned qty reached? order terminal?) is a modelling choice for sim-v5, not something this descriptor may improvise. When it lands, bind status to final_confirmation via valueMap and EXTEND the profile enum against a paginated measurement. --- 2026-08-03 (SAME DAY, LATER): status IS BOUND AGAIN, THIS TIME DERIVED. Earlier today I removed the { const: 'fertig' } binding and wrote that the root cause 'is not fixed here' and that 'a BDE system in which no confirmation is EVER final never reports an operation complete'. THE SECOND HALF OF THAT WAS WRONG: erp.order_operations held 111,827 rows at FINAL_CONFIRMED on prod at the time. The operations really do close; only the CONFIRMATION FLAG was unwired, and it was unwired by a literal — factory-bde-bridge wrote FALSE seventy lines above the very UPDATE that performs the FINAL_CONFIRMED transition, throwing away the rowCount that IS the discriminator. Fixed in sim-v5 aa9c1457 and live on .154; measured after, 1 of 254 confirmations in five minutes now carries final_confirmation = true, which is the one that reached planned_qty. So status is now a DERIVATION from a field that really discriminates: final_confirmation true -> 'fertig' (this confirmation closed the operation), false -> 'in_arbeit' (more work to come). That is not the same act as the constant it replaces: a valueMap over a field that only ever holds one value would have been the same lie wearing a derivation's clothes, which is exactly why the binding was removed rather than re-pointed this morning. --- 2026-08-03, THIRD ENTRY, AND A CORRECTION TO THE SECOND. The paragraph above justified this binding with '1 of 254 confirmations in five minutes carries final_confirmation = true'. That measurement was real but it was taken on the WRONG URL: /api/confirmations, the raw list. THIS SOURCE POLLS /api/confirmations?per_po=true (see connection.path, idProperty production_order_no) -- the per-production-order AGGREGATE -- and there final_confirmation was the literal true, typed as the literal true and hardcoded in the mapper. Measured: true on 100 of 100 rows. So for a few hours this 'derivation' produced 'fertig' for every record, which is the SAME falsehood the { const: 'fertig' } it replaced was removed for. THE LESSON, and it is the third time in one day: measure the projection the CONSUMER reads, not a neighbouring one that happens to answer. Every check passed, on the wrong endpoint. Fixed in sim-v5 15e19e04 -- the aggregate now derives it as BOOL_AND(status IN ('FINAL_CONFIRMED','CANCELLED')) over erp.order_operations, the same predicate apply-operation-complete.ts uses, with a PO that has no operation rows yielding FALSE rather than TRUE. MEASURED AFTER, end to end: the prod aggregate returns 4167 true / 833 false over 5000 rows, and business_events now carries status 'fertig' 2393 and 'in_arbeit' 2068 where it had been 100 % 'fertig'. The binding is finally what it claims. CAPT-RETRACT 2026-08-18 - PHASE-2 CHARACTERISATION, no functional change in this commit. This source ALREADY declares polling.paginate true, so its DATA-7 refusal is NOT the unpaginated_full_refresh family the other four sources were in: measured on .99, osf-it-edge-erp refuses it with reason filtered_path:per_po, 4 times in a 30-minute window. That reason comes from assessPathScope, whose rule is deliberately crude and fail-closed - ANY query parameter in connection.path is presumed population-narrowing until it is declared in polling.nonFilteringParams. The declared path is /api/confirmations?per_po=true, so per_po trips it. MEASURED, because the-path-narrows was a presumption and not a finding: per_po=true is an AGGREGATION, not a filter. Upstream it is GROUP BY b.production_order_no over logistics.bde_confirmations, which holds 3,148,265 raw confirmation rows carrying 42,040 distinct production_order_no. Paged the way it-edge pages (limit 5000, advance by rows returned, stop on an empty page): 10 pages, 42,040 rows, 42,040 distinct production_order_no, 0 duplicates - EXACTLY the 42,040 distinct production orders in the table. Both limit and offset are honoured (offset=60000 -> 0 rows), with /api/orders?limit=5 -> 5 as the positive control in the same run. So for the entity this source actually publishes - one OperationsResponse per production order, keyed on production_order_no - the population IS provably complete and is exhausted exactly. TWO CAVEATS, named rather than waved away: the upstream statement also carries WHERE b.cancelled_at IS NULL, which TODAY excludes nothing (measured: 0 cancelled rows, and 42,040 distinct production_order_no both with and without the predicate) but IS a latent narrowing that would silently shrink the population the moment cancellations appear; and the aggregate HAVING clause is empty only because the declared path passes no machine filter. PROPOSAL, deliberately NOT applied here: the correct change is to add per_po to polling.nonFilteringParams - a reviewable one-line exception in the SSOT, which is exactly what that field exists for - and NOT a pagination change, since paginate is already true. It should be made together with a decision about cancelled_at, because a retraction licensed by this feed would then also propagate every-confirmation-for-this-order-was-cancelled as this-OperationsResponse-no-longer-exists. That may well be right, but it is a semantic call for a steward, not a lint fix.
